evidence: src/application/dto/ProjectDto.ts declares CreateProjectInput, ProjectDto and toProjectDto(project: Project), following the input + DTO + mapper pattern.
src/application/dto/UserDto.ts declares CreateUserInput, UserDto and toUserDto(user: User), the same pattern as ProjectDto.ts.
src/application/dto/TaskDto.ts declares TaskDto and toTaskDto(task: Task). This is the only place dueDate becomes ISO-or-null (task.dueDate?.toIso() ?? null) and assigneeId becomes null.
src/application/dto/TaskInputs.ts declares AddTaskInput, AssignTaskInput, ListProjectTasksInput and MarkTaskDoneInput. These are plain input contracts with no logic, so no rule is duplicated.
Minor layout inconsistency: Task inputs have their own file, while Project and User inputs sit next to their DTOs. The concern is the same, so the module still holds together.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All four files handle one concern: the application layer's data contracts. Each one either describes what a use case accepts (an input interface) or what it returns (an output DTO). The output files follow one pattern: a `<Entity>Dto` interface plus a pure `to<Entity>Dto(entity)` mapper. Each mapping rule lives in one place only, and no file skips the module's own abstractions.

There is one small layout inconsistency. Project and User keep their create-input next to their DTO. Task's inputs sit in a separate file, `TaskInputs.ts`, probably because there are four of them. Files are organised differently, but the purpose doesn't split, so this doesn't count as a fail.

`ProjectDto` and `UserDto` have the same shape (id and name). They describe different concepts, though, and carry no shared rule, so this isn't duplication. Task-to-DTO formatting, such as `dueDate` to ISO-or-null and `assigneeId` to null, happens only in `toTaskDto`. The `dueDate` format is documented once, on `AddTaskInput`.
